tools.name: GetConversationMetadata
tools.description:
Get metadata of a Channel, a Direct Message (IM / DM) or a Multi-Person (MPIM) conversation.

Use this tool to retrieve metadata about a conversation with a conversation_id, a channel name,
or by the user_id(s), username(s), and/or email(s) of the user(s) in the conversation.

This tool does not return the messages in a conversation.

Provide exactly one of:
- conversation_id; or
- channel_name; or
- any combination of user_ids, usernames, and/or emails.

parameters.name: conversation_id
parameters.description: The ID of the conversation to get metadata for. Defaults to identifying the conversation another way.

parameters.name: channel_name
parameters.description: The name of the channel to get metadata for. Prefer providing a conversation_id, when available, since the performance is better. Defaults to identifying the conversation another way.

parameters.name: usernames
parameters.description: The names of the users to get the conversation metadata, each matched case-insensitively against the Slack handle, real name, and display name. A value matching several people, or only a real or display name, is not acted on directly; the tool returns the matching users so the call can be retried with the user ID or email. Prefer user_ids and/or emails when available, since the performance is better. Defaults to no usernames.

parameters.name: emails
parameters.description: The emails of the users to get the conversation metadata. Defaults to no emails.

parameters.name: user_ids
parameters.description: The IDs of the users to get the conversation metadata. Defaults to no user IDs.

tools.name: GetMessages
tools.description:
Get messages in a Slack Channel, DM (direct message) or MPIM (multi-person) conversation.

Provide exactly one of:
- conversation_id; or
- channel_name; or
- any combination of user_ids, usernames, and/or emails.

To filter messages by an absolute datetime, use 'oldest_datetime' and/or 'latest_datetime'. If
only 'oldest_datetime' is provided, it will return messages from the oldest_datetime to the
current time. If only 'latest_datetime' is provided, it will return messages since the
beginning of the conversation to the latest_datetime.

To filter messages by a relative datetime, use 'oldest_relative' and/or 'latest_relative'
with numeric `DD:HH:MM` offsets only. Convert relative phrases to `DD:HH:MM` before calling
this tool. If only 'oldest_relative' is provided, it will return messages from the
oldest_relative to the current time. If only 'latest_relative' is provided, it will return
messages from the current time to the latest_relative.

Do not provide both 'oldest_datetime' and 'oldest_relative' or both 'latest_datetime' and
'latest_relative'.

Leave all arguments with the default None to get messages without date/time filtering

parameters.name: conversation_id
parameters.description: The ID of the conversation to get messages from. Provide exactly one of conversation_id OR any combination of user_ids, usernames, and/or emails. Defaults to identifying the conversation another way.

parameters.name: channel_name
parameters.description: The name of the channel to get messages from. Prefer providing a conversation_id, when available, since the performance is better. Defaults to identifying the conversation another way.

parameters.name: user_ids
parameters.description: The IDs of the users in the conversation to get messages from. Defaults to no user IDs.

parameters.name: usernames
parameters.description: The names of the users in the conversation to get messages from, each matched case-insensitively against the Slack handle, real name, and display name. A value matching several people, or only a real or display name, is not acted on directly; the tool returns the matching users so the call can be retried with the user ID or email. Prefer user_ids and/or emails when available, since the performance is better. Defaults to no usernames.

parameters.name: emails
parameters.description: The emails of the users in the conversation to get messages from. Defaults to no emails.

parameters.name: oldest_relative
parameters.description: The oldest message to include in the results, specified as a time offset from the current time. Use only the numeric 'DD:HH:MM' format; convert relative phrases to that format before calling this tool. Defaults to no lower bound.

parameters.name: latest_relative
parameters.description: The latest message to include in the results, specified as a time offset from the current time. Use only the numeric 'DD:HH:MM' format; convert relative phrases to that format before calling this tool. Defaults to no upper bound.

parameters.name: oldest_datetime
parameters.description: The oldest message to include in the results, specified as a datetime object in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' or ISO 8601. Defaults to no lower bound.

parameters.name: latest_datetime
parameters.description: The latest message to include in the results, specified as a datetime object in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' or ISO 8601. Defaults to no upper bound.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of messages to return. Maximum is 100. Defaults to 20.

parameters.name: next_cursor
parameters.description: The cursor to use for pagination. Defaults to the first page.

output.description: The messages in a Slack Channel, DM (direct message) or MPIM (multi-person) conversation.

tools.name: GetThreadMessages
tools.description:
Get messages in a Slack thread.

A thread is a collection of messages grouped together as replies to a parent message.
This tool retrieves all messages in a specific thread, identified by the parent message's
timestamp (thread_ts).

Provide exactly one of:
- conversation_id; or
- channel_name; or
- any combination of user_ids, usernames, and/or emails.

To filter messages by an absolute datetime, use 'oldest_datetime' and/or 'latest_datetime'. If
only 'oldest_datetime' is provided, it will return messages from the oldest_datetime to the
current time. If only 'latest_datetime' is provided, it will return messages since the
beginning of the thread to the latest_datetime.

To filter messages by a relative datetime, use 'oldest_relative' and/or 'latest_relative'
with numeric `DD:HH:MM` offsets only. Convert relative phrases to `DD:HH:MM` before calling
this tool. If only 'oldest_relative' is provided, it will return messages from the
oldest_relative to the current time. If only 'latest_relative' is provided, it will return
messages from the current time to the latest_relative.

Do not provide both 'oldest_datetime' and 'oldest_relative' or both 'latest_datetime' and
'latest_relative'.

Leave all datetime arguments with the default None to get all thread messages without
date/time filtering.

parameters.name: thread_ts
parameters.description: The timestamp of the parent message that starts the thread. This is the 'ts' field from the parent message.

parameters.name: conversation_id
parameters.description: The ID of the conversation containing the thread. Provide exactly one of conversation_id OR channel_name OR any combination of user_ids, usernames, and/or emails. Defaults to identifying the conversation another way.

parameters.name: channel_name
parameters.description: The name of the channel containing the thread. Prefer providing a conversation_id, when available, since the performance is better. Defaults to identifying the conversation another way.

parameters.name: user_ids
parameters.description: The IDs of the users in the conversation containing the thread. Defaults to no user IDs.

parameters.name: usernames
parameters.description: The names of the users in the conversation containing the thread, each matched case-insensitively against the Slack handle, real name, and display name. A value matching several people, or only a real or display name, is not acted on directly; the tool returns the matching users so the call can be retried with the user ID or email. Prefer user_ids and/or emails when available, since the performance is better. Defaults to no usernames.

parameters.name: emails
parameters.description: The emails of the users in the conversation containing the thread. Defaults to no emails.

parameters.name: oldest_relative
parameters.description: The oldest message to include in the results, specified as a time offset from the current time. Use only the numeric 'DD:HH:MM' format; convert relative phrases to that format before calling this tool. Defaults to no lower bound.

parameters.name: latest_relative
parameters.description: The latest message to include in the results, specified as a time offset from the current time. Use only the numeric 'DD:HH:MM' format; convert relative phrases to that format before calling this tool. Defaults to no upper bound.

parameters.name: oldest_datetime
parameters.description: The oldest message to include in the results, specified as a datetime object in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' or ISO 8601. Defaults to no lower bound.

parameters.name: latest_datetime
parameters.description: The latest message to include in the results, specified as a datetime object in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' or ISO 8601. Defaults to no upper bound.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of messages to return. Maximum is 100. Defaults to 20.

parameters.name: next_cursor
parameters.description: The cursor to use for pagination. Defaults to the first page.

tools.name: GetUsersInfo
tools.description:
Get the information of one or more users in Slack by ID, username, and/or email.

Provide any combination of user_ids, usernames, and/or emails. If you need to retrieve
data about multiple users, DO NOT CALL THE TOOL MULTIPLE TIMES. Instead, call it once
with all the user_ids, usernames, and/or emails.

Do not retrieve users' info first to get the metadata or messages of a conversation,
as it is inefficient: conversations can be looked up by user_ids, usernames, and/or
emails directly.

A name can match several people, and every match is returned. Prefer user_ids and/or emails when available, since the performance is better. Defaults to no usernames.

tools.name: InviteUsersToChannel
tools.description:
Invite users to a Slack channel or MPIM (multi-person direct message).

This tool invites specified users to join a Slack conversation. It works with:
- Public channels
- Private channels
- MPIMs (multi-person direct messages / group DMs)

You can specify users by their user IDs, usernames, or email addresses.

Provide exactly one of channel_id or channel_name, and at least one of user_ids, usernames,
or emails.

The tool will resolve usernames and emails to user IDs before inviting them.
Up to 100 users may be invited at once.

parameters.name: channel_id
parameters.description: The ID of the Slack channel or MPIM (multi-person direct message) to invite users to. Provide exactly one of channel_id OR channel_name. Defaults to identifying the channel another way.

parameters.name: channel_name
parameters.description: The name of the channel to invite users to. Prefer providing a channel_id when available for better performance. Note: MPIMs don't have names, so use channel_id for MPIMs. Defaults to identifying the channel another way.

parameters.name: user_ids
parameters.description: The Slack user IDs of the people to invite. Up to 100 users may be listed. Provide at least one of user_ids, usernames, or emails. Defaults to no user IDs.

parameters.name: usernames
parameters.description: The names of the people to invite, each matched case-insensitively against the Slack handle, real name, and display name. A value matching several people, or only a real or display name, is not acted on directly; the tool returns the matching users so the call can be retried with the user ID or email. Prefer user_ids and/or emails when available, since the performance is better. Defaults to no usernames.

parameters.name: emails
parameters.description: The email addresses of the people to invite. Defaults to no emails.

output.description: The response from inviting users to the conversation

tools.name: ReactToMessage
tools.description:
Add or remove the user's emoji reaction on a message in a Slack conversation.

Provide exactly one of conversation_id or channel_name.

Only the user's own reaction is added or removed; other people's reactions are left
untouched. Adding a reaction the user already left, or removing one they have not left,
changes nothing and is reported with changed set to false.

parameters.name: message_ts
parameters.description: The timestamp of the message to react to. This is the 'ts' field of the message. To react to a reply in a thread, use the reply's own 'ts'.

parameters.name: emoji
parameters.description: The Slack name of the emoji, with or without the surrounding colons. Custom workspace emoji are referenced by name the same way.

parameters.name: conversation_id
parameters.description: The ID of the conversation (Channel, DM/IM, or MPIM) containing the message. Defaults to identifying the conversation another way.

parameters.name: channel_name
parameters.description: The name of the channel containing the message. Prefer providing a conversation_id, when available, since the performance is better. Defaults to identifying the conversation another way.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Whether to add or remove the reaction. Defaults to 'add'.

output.description: The result of the reaction change

tools.name: SendMessage
tools.description:
Send a message to a Channel, Direct Message (IM/DM), or Multi-Person (MPIM) conversation.

Can send top-level messages or reply to an existing thread.

Provide exactly one of:
- channel_name; or
- conversation_id; or
- any combination of user_ids, usernames, and/or emails.

In case multiple user_ids, usernames, and/or emails are provided, the tool will open a
multi-person conversation with the specified people and send the message to it.

To reply to a thread, also provide thread_ts (the 'ts' field of the parent message).
Optionally set reply_broadcast to true to also post the reply to the main conversation.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: The content of the message to send.

parameters.name: channel_name
parameters.description: The channel name to send the message to. Prefer providing a conversation_id, when available, since the performance is better. Defaults to identifying the conversation another way.

parameters.name: conversation_id
parameters.description: The conversation ID to send the message to. Defaults to identifying the conversation another way.

parameters.name: user_ids
parameters.description: The Slack user IDs of the people to message. Defaults to no user IDs.

parameters.name: emails
parameters.description: The emails of the people to message. Defaults to no emails.

parameters.name: usernames
parameters.description: The names of the people to message, each matched case-insensitively against the Slack handle, real name, and display name. A value matching several people, or only a real or display name, is not acted on directly; the tool returns the matching users so the call can be retried with the user ID or email. Prefer user_ids and/or emails when available, since the performance is better. Defaults to no usernames.

parameters.name: thread_ts
parameters.description: The timestamp of the parent message to reply to in a thread. Use the 'ts' field from the parent message (the first message in the thread), not from a reply. Get this value from previously retrieved conversation or thread messages. Defaults to sending a new top-level message.

parameters.name: reply_broadcast
parameters.description: When replying to a thread (thread_ts is set), set to true to also post the reply to the main conversation. Only valid when thread_ts is provided. Defaults to False

output.description: The response from the Slack API

documentationChunks.content:
<Callout type="info" title="Channel creation not supported">
Managing channels in Slack requires the `channels:manage` scope, which is only available with bot tokens. Arcade uses user tokens (the type of token Arcade supports), so creating new channels is not possible with this toolkit. You can invite users to an existing channel, but channel creation is not supported.
</Callout>

summary:
The Slack toolkit integrates Arcade with Slack's API, enabling LLMs to read, send, and manage Slack messages, channels, and users on behalf of authenticated users.

## Capabilities

- **Message access & threading** — Retrieve channel, DM, and MPIM messages with flexible absolute or relative datetime filtering; read full thread reply chains by parent timestamp.
- **Sending & reacting** — Post top-level messages or thread replies to any channel, DM, or MPIM resolved by ID, name, or user identifiers; add or remove emoji reactions on individual messages.
- **Conversation & membership management** — List all conversations the user belongs to, fetch conversation metadata, retrieve member lists, and invite users (up to 100 at once) to channels or MPIMs.
- **User lookup** — Resolve one or many users by ID, username, or email in a single call; list the full team roster; fetch the authenticated user's own profile via `WhoAmI`.

## OAuth

This toolkit uses OAuth 2.0 delegated auth via Slack. See the [Arcade Slack auth provider docs](https://docs.arcade.dev/en/references/auth-providers/slack) for setup details.
